newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Nov 2 Initial Claims from 331,000, Nov 2 4-Week Average from 333,500, Oct 26 Continued Claims from 2,488,000 and Oct 19 from 2,437,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast jobless claims filings of 334,000 in the November 9 week.
The department said four states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended November 2, the latest period for which the data are available.
They were California, with 6,779; Wisconsin, with 2,099; South Carolina, with 1,190; and Arkansas, with 1,030.
California reported layoffs in the construction industry and in agriculture. Wisconsin cited layoffs in construction, trade, service industries, and in manufacturing.
South Carolina had layoffs in the industrial machinery industry. Arkansas reported layoffs in the lumber and rubber industries.
Two states reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 in the latest week.
They were Michigan, with 3,482 fewer filings, and Kansas, with 1,005. Michigan reported fewer layoffs in the automobile industry. Kansas gave no comment.
